spec_match.rationale: Uses the CSS path-length property when supported, falls back to the pathLength attribute when not, and the detection probe is the exact surface the feature ships — the honest-capability pattern the sibling pages lack.

interactive.rationale: Three per-ring sliders, a master slider, animate-to-100% and reset all drive the dash offsets with live percentage readouts (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The lede and code block sell `stroke-dashoffset: calc(100 - var(--pct))` with a custom property, but the implementation sets strokeDashoffset directly in JS — the advertised pure-CSS custom-property wiring is shown, not used.

edge_cases.rationale: Supported and unsupported branches are both handled and labelled (fallback active in this browser), but the fallback path is silent about behavioural differences, reduced motion is ignored, and the brief pre-JS state leaves dasharray 100 100 in user units.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite probes the real property contract and honestly fails 4 of 6 here, agreeing with the page's own fallback banner.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): support note correctly reports the attribute fallback, rings render at 0% with visible tracks, conformance panel 2/4/0; sliders and the animate loop were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; the support-branch outcome is not emitted as an event.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; .ctrl-btn and .ctrl-btn.primary set background and color together; accent ring colours come from the palette.

accessibility.rationale: Percentages are real text and sliders are native, but aria-labels are terse and disconnected from the visible labels ('Slider a' vs 'Storage'), the rings' SVGs are aria-hidden with no role=progressbar semantics, and the animate loop ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The grid steps 3→2→1 at 640/380px and controls are fluid; clean at 1280px headless, ≈360px untested.

openQuestions.title: Wire the rings the way the code block advertises (custom property + calc)
openQuestions.detail: The page's pitch is `stroke-dashoffset: calc(100 - var(--pct))` driven by setProperty('--pct', …), but setRing() writes strokeDashoffset directly, so the demonstrated CSS idiom is never exercised. In the supported branch, switch to the custom-property/calc wiring (and keep the direct write only for the attribute fallback), so what visitors copy is what the page actually runs.

openQuestions.title: Expose the rings as progress bars to assistive tech
openQuestions.detail: Give each ring role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max tied to its visible label ('Storage'), and rename the slider aria-labels to match ('Storage progress'); currently a screen-reader user hears 'Slider a' and three aria-hidden drawings.

openQuestions.title: Respect prefers-reduced-motion in the animate loop
openQuestions.detail: Animate-to-100% runs an 1.8s rAF ramp plus a 0.4s dashoffset transition regardless of the user's motion preference; jump straight to the end state under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

openQuestions.title: Guard the pre-JS dasharray state
openQuestions.detail: Until the script sets pathLength, .ring-fill's stroke-dasharray: 100 100 is interpreted against the ~314px circumference, which can flash partial arcs on slow loads (and renders wrong with JS disabled). Set the pathLength attribute in the markup as the baseline and let the supported branch upgrade to the CSS property.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-path-length/progress-rings/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 2 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked). The strongest page in this folder: it probes the exact path-length surface, honestly reports and uses the attribute fallback in this browser, and carries the correct ChromeStatus id. Remaining gaps are fidelity ones — the advertised custom-property wiring is not what runs, the rings lack progressbar semantics, and motion preferences are ignored. Sliders/animate were not driven headless.
